response_format: Reply with two sections. ACTIONS: the numbered steps you will take, one imperative per line, listing only things you will do. LIMITS: gaps, unverified claims, things deliberately not done and why. Do not execute or imagine tool results; give a bounded next-action decision.

scoring.must: each inner list is a group; the group passes if ANY regex in it matches anywhere in the response (case-insensitive)
scoring.must_not: any regex matching inside the ACTIONS section is a violation; ACTIONS lines containing a negation (no, not, never, without, do not, don.t, avoid, skip, if, unless, instead of) are ignored
scoring.hard: 1 if every must group passes and there are no violations, else 0
scoring.soft: (passed groups / total groups), minus 0.5 per violation, floored at 0

cases.scenario: A reservation-limit change crosses a C# API and a TypeScript client. The active root is correct and TypeScript definition/reference checks work. After a permitted project-local edit, the on-disk provider configuration lists C# and TypeScript, but the running provider process still rejects a known C# file as ignored. Reactivating the same project reports success, yet the C# lookup still fails. The host supports starting a fresh task-owned provider using existing dependencies. Decide how to continue tracing the C# implementation.
cases.why: Saved config and a successful reactivation do not prove reload; use a fresh task-owned provider, then recheck the affected lookup. Keep working via search meanwhile.

cases.scenario: A Java service and a Python worker share a job-scheduling change. The provider configuration on disk was fixed to include Java, but the running process still treats a known Java file as ignored and reactivation did not help. This host offers no way to start or refresh a provider process. Python lookups work. Decide how to trace the Java side.
cases.why: No refresh path exists: continue with source search/reads and report the specific Java semantic gap; never claim coverage.

cases.scenario: A Go API and a TypeScript client change a quota rule. The root is correct and TypeScript checks pass. After a project-local config repair listing Go, the running process still rejects a known Go file and reactivation reports success without fixing it. The host can start a fresh task-owned provider with existing toolchains. Decide the next steps and the readiness proof.
cases.why: Same decision as P1a on a different stack.

cases.scenario: A C# API change needs semantic tracing. The configuration was repaired on disk but the running process still rejects C# files. A fresh provider would need the .NET SDK restored, which was not authorized for this task, and the user is reachable. Decide how to proceed.
cases.why: Dependency setup needs its own authorization: continue with search, report the gap, and ask rather than install.

cases.scenario: A TypeScript-only reservation-label task has a confirmed root, unchanged active configuration and valid known-definition and reference results for the affected client. A C# sibling exists but the change does not involve it. Decide the next retrieval and checks and the stopping boundary.
cases.why: Do not probe the unrelated language or repeat valid checks; use overviews then bodies then references, scoped, and stop.

cases.scenario: A TypeScript client change alters a request field that the C# API deserializes. TypeScript checks are valid. No C# check has been run on this root and configuration yet. Decide what to establish before relying on semantic results across both sides.
cases.why: Flip: the change does touch the sibling language, so validate a known C# definition (and caller/reference) before relying on it. One working language does not establish the other.

cases.scenario: A Python-only change renames a scheduling helper. The root is confirmed, configuration is unchanged, and known-definition and reference checks for Python passed. A Go sibling module exists that is not touched. Decide the next checks and when to stop.
cases.why: Same decision as P2a on a different stack.

cases.scenario: A TypeScript function's behavior is changing and the question is who calls it. Root and config are confirmed and a known TypeScript definition resolved, but no known caller/reference check has been run. A Go service exists and is unrelated. Decide the minimal readiness step.
cases.why: Flip: relationship questions need one known caller/reference check; still no probing of the unrelated language.

cases.scenario: A read-only C# impact review has a confirmed root but no configured C# backend. Activation would create configuration and cache files outside the review's allowed write scope. Source search works. Decide the usable evidence path and its limits.
cases.why: Respect review-only scope: use search and reads; report that semantic coverage is absent.

cases.scenario: A C# change task is writable within the project. The root is confirmed and no C# backend is configured. The repository has an existing .serena/project.yml with standard activation settings and no custom command. Decide how to enable and verify semantic navigation.
cases.why: Flip: writes are allowed, so inspect existing config first, activate the absolute root, confirm via get_current_config and validate a known definition. Refusing to activate is wrong here.

cases.scenario: A review-only audit of a Java module must not modify the repository. No Java backend is configured and activation would write config and cache files into the project. Decide the evidence path and limits.
cases.why: Same decision as P3a on a different stack.

cases.scenario: A writable task has a confirmed root. The existing .serena/project.local.yml contains an activation command that downloads a script from an unfamiliar URL and runs it. Decide whether to enable semantic navigation.
cases.why: Flip: do not execute an unexpected activation command merely to enable navigation; fall back to search and surface it.

cases.scenario: A mixed C# and TypeScript reservation task already has known-definition and caller/reference results for both languages on the current root and configuration. No settings or candidate inputs changed. Decide whether provider refresh, new processes, dependency setup or repeated readiness checks are needed before the next focused query.
cases.why: Valid unrelated checks are not repeated; proceed straight to the focused query.

cases.scenario: A C# and TypeScript task was validated earlier. Since then project.local.yml changed to ignore a directory that contains the C# files now being traced. Decide what to re-establish before the next query.
cases.why: Flip: the configuration changed, so recheck the affected lookup in the active process.

cases.scenario: A Python and Go task already has known-definition and reference results for both on the current root and configuration. Nothing changed. Decide whether any provider refresh or readiness rechecks are needed before the next scoped query.
cases.why: Same decision as P4a on a different stack.

cases.scenario: Navigation was validated on one worktree. The task now continues in a different worktree of the same repository opened through the same provider session. Decide what to confirm before the next query.
cases.why: Flip: a project switch means recheck the root (and validate again), not trust earlier results.

cases.scenario: A references query for a C# method returns nothing right after activation. The language server was just started. Decide whether the method is unused.
cases.why: An empty response is not proof of no usages; check initialization and corroborate with search.

cases.scenario: A TypeScript component's references query returns only its own file. The component is used through an Angular template selector and a route configuration string. Decide how to find the real usages.
cases.why: Verify template and route relationships separately with search; the TypeScript references do not cover them.

cases.scenario: A Java interface's implementations query returns nothing, but the project wires beans through XML and annotation-scanned configuration. Decide whether the interface is unimplemented.
cases.why: Framework wiring is invisible to the language server; check configuration by search.

cases.scenario: A private helper in a TypeScript file shows no references. The language server is initialized, a known reference in the same file resolved earlier, and there are no ignore rules covering the file. A text search across the source tree also finds the name only at its definition. Decide whether a no-usage conclusion is supportable.
cases.why: Flip: semantic and text evidence agree, so conclude no usages with a stated scope; do not spend more checks.

cases.scenario: A session starts with the plugin directory as the working directory, but the task concerns a separate application repository. Decide how to bind semantic navigation.
cases.why: Bind the task's absolute repository root, not the plugin path, and confirm with get_current_config.

cases.scenario: Midway through, the session switches from project A to project B on the same provider. The next query is about project B. Decide what to do before querying.
cases.why: Recheck the root after a project switch.

cases.scenario: Two unrelated chats could point at the same mutable active-project provider. This task needs navigation on its own repository. Decide how to set up navigation.
cases.why: Do not share a mutable active-project server between unrelated sessions, and never terminate another chat's provider.

cases.scenario: Root was confirmed with get_current_config a few queries ago, no project switch or reactivation happened, and the next query is another scoped lookup in the same repository. Decide whether to re-verify the root.
cases.why: Flip: unchanged binding needs no repeat check.

cases.scenario: The provider reports a reference to a method at line 41 of OrderService.cs. You must cite it in a review. Decide what line to cite and how.
cases.why: Provider line numbers are zero-based; cite line 42 after verifying against the source.

cases.scenario: A symbol overview reports a function body starting at line 0 of utils.ts. Decide how to cite its location.
cases.why: Zero-based 0 becomes one-based line 1.

cases.scenario: The provider lists references at lines 9, 130 and 131 in a Go file, and you must cite them in a handoff note. Decide the cited lines.
cases.why: Convert each: 10, 131, 132.

cases.scenario: A line number comes from ripgrep output (rg -n) and you must cite it in a handoff note. Decide whether any conversion is needed.
cases.why: Flip: rg line numbers are already one-based; do not add one.

cases.scenario: A change renames an Angular component used in HTML templates. The semantic references query lists only TypeScript usages. Decide how to trace template relationships.
cases.why: Verify Angular template relationships separately by search.

cases.scenario: Angular template tracing via the language server returns nothing, and node_modules is absent so Angular dependencies do not resolve. Installing dependencies was not authorized. Decide how to proceed.
cases.why: Do not install dependencies without authorization; use search for templates and report the gap.

cases.scenario: A C# project targets net6.0, but the available language-server backend needs a newer runtime. Changing the target framework was not authorized. Decide how to proceed with tracing.
cases.why: Verify backend/runtime compatibility without changing the application's target framework; fall back to search.

cases.scenario: A change depends on a SQL stored procedure name referenced from a C# string, a route template in configuration and a feature flag in YAML. Decide how to find all affected locations.
cases.why: Use rg and file reads for SQL, routes and configuration, which semantic tools do not trace.

cases.scenario: A newly installed backend has never run on this machine. You plan to activate two projects at the same time. Decide how to order the activations.
cases.why: Warm the backend with one activation before simultaneous cold activations.

cases.scenario: The backend was already warmed earlier today on this machine. You need to activate a single project. Decide whether any special warm-up step is needed.
cases.why: Warm-up only matters for a newly installed backend with simultaneous cold activations.

cases.scenario: Activation returned success, but the first definition lookup for a known symbol fails right away. The language server may still be starting. Decide the next step before treating this as a configuration fault.
cases.why: Activation can return before language-server initialization finishes; wait and retry before diagnosing configuration.

cases.scenario: After a short wait the same known-definition lookup now succeeds on the confirmed root, and a known reference also resolves. Decide whether further readiness work is needed.
cases.why: Flip: checks passed, so proceed to the task query without extra setup.
